ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, L, M, N are on the same horizontal line segment, LM is labeled 10, MN is labeled 10, so M is located at the midpoint of LN. Point P is directly below M, and there is a right-angle mark where PM and LN intersect, indicating that PM is perpendicular to LN. The hypotenuse PL is labeled 2x - 4, and the hypotenuse PN is labeled x + 5. The problem asks to find NP. Reasoning: Because LM = MN = 10, M is the midpoint of LN; also because PM is perpendicular to LN, PM is the perpendicular bisector of LN. Point P is on the perpendicular bisector, so the distances from P to L and N are equal, that is, PL = PN. Therefore 2x - 4 = x + 5, solving gives x = 9. NP = x + 5 = 9 + 5 = 14.

method.method_draft: From the image, read that L, M, and N lie on the same horizontal segment with LM = 10 and MN = 10, so M is the midpoint of LN. Also read that PM meets LN at a right angle, so PM is the perpendicular bisector of LN. The side labels show PL = 2x - 4 and PN = x + 5. From the text, the target is to find NP. Use the perpendicular bisector theorem: any point P on the perpendicular bisector of LN is equidistant from L and N, so PL = PN. Set 2x - 4 = x + 5, solve x = 9, then NP = x + 5 = 14.
